intro: Professionals and everyday users convert bars (bar) to psi (psi) when working across metric and imperial standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One bar equals 14.503774 psi, while 1 pounds per square inch equals 0.068948 bars. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between bar and psi. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many psi (psi) are in 1 bar (bar)?
faqs.answer: There are 14.50377377 psi (psi) in 1 bar (bar), which rounds to 14.5038 psi for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pounds per square inch equals 0.068948 bars.

faqs.question: How do I convert bars to psi (bar to psi)?
faqs.answer: To convert bars to psi, use the formula: psi = bar × 14.50377377. For example, converting 2.2 bar gives 31.9083 psi.

faqs.question: What is 2.2 bars in psi?
faqs.answer: 2.2 bars (bar) equals exactly 31.9083 psi (psi) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
